symptom: Under true-right-false-down, nested decisions' ELSE columns formed a staircase: each outer column started under the last element of every column inside it (no C at y=660, no B 870, no A 1080 with the decisions at y=200), though each column has its own x. layout flows --dry-run called it already laid out.
cause: The column's top was BranchGap under the TRUE body's whole measured height, and that height includes the columns of IFs nested in the TRUE body, which stand right of this column.
fix: The column starts on the first row under the decision unless an object the TRUE body actually drew (built before the ELSE, so its positions are known) stands in the column's band — half an activity left of the split to the measured column width plus laneGap — then BranchGap under the lowest such object.
insight: Measured bounds are a box; deciding clearance from them stacks anything nested. The TRUE body is built first, so the real objects are there to test against — the same move the guard line already made with objectsExtent. The measurer's height stays an upper bound, which only reserves room.
test: flowlayout_ifelse_column_test.go TestIfElseColumn_NestedElseColumnsShareTheFirstRow failed with the issue's exact staircase (300/660/870/1080); control TestIfElseColumn_ElseColumnStillClearsTheThenBody and the existing NestedColumnInTheTrueBodyIsCleared fail with overlaps when the band test is stubbed. Live 11.17.0: issue repro puts every false branch at y=300, describe prints no positions, second exec unchanged, mx check 0 errors.
